problem:
Find an eigenvector of $A=[\begin{aligned}-14 & 12 & 3 \\ -20 & 17 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2.$

examples.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-2.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]-(-2)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 0=0 \\ {x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $3$rd). Thus, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain $x_3=0.$ Substituting this in the first equation, we get $x_1=-x_2.$ Therefore, the general solution is

feedback.problem:
$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & -7 \\ 12 & -8 & 6 \\ 12 & -10 & 8\end{aligned}]
$$

The vector $v$ and the matrix $A$ are given above. 
If $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2,$ then what is the value of $\frac{a}{c}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =2.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 5 & -7 \\ 12 & -8 & 6 \\ 12 & -10 & 8\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 & -7 \\ 12 & -10 & 6 \\ 12 & -10 & 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors corresponding to this eigenvalue, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}-7{x}_{3}=0 \\ 12{x}_{1}-10{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=0 \\ 12{x}_{1}-10{x}_{2}+6{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 & -7 & 0 \\ 12 & -10 & 6 & 0 \\ 12 & -10 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -15 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -15 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -15 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are two pivot columns (the $1$st and the $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we obtain ${x}_{2}=3{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =-\frac{1}{4}(-5{x}_{2}+7{x}_{3}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(-5(3{x}_{3})+7{x}_{3}) \\  & =2{x}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ 3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting, for instance, ${x}_{3}=1,$ we get the following eigenvector:

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Finally, $\frac{a}{c}=\frac{2}{1}=2.$
